en.title: Filmmaker Walks Through L.A. Firestorm's Ashes, Hopes for Dialogue
en.summary: Austrian director Lukas Marxt captured the devastating aftermath of the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires. His documentary, '>1.5°C: Pyropolitics and the New World,' aims to ignite crucial conversations about climate change and its tangible impacts.
en.body:
The infernos that ravaged Los Angeles in 2025 were not just a news cycle event; they were a visceral, terrifying reality for many. Austrian filmmaker **Lukas Marxt** ventured into the heart of this destruction, documenting the "apocalyptic surrounding" left in the wake of the devastating wildfires. His latest film, **'>1.5°C: Pyropolitics and the New World,'** premieres at prestigious festivals like DOK Leipzig and Viennale, before heading to IDFA, offering a unflinching look at the aftermath.

Marxt's work is known for its observational style, drawing audiences into complex realities with a quiet intensity. This film, however, delves into a particularly harrowing subject, forcing viewers to confront the tangible consequences of climate change. While the film focuses on the L.A. fires, its implications resonate far beyond Southern California, touching on broader global environmental anxieties. The title itself, referencing the critical 1.5°C warming threshold, underscores the film's thematic core: a direct confrontation with the escalating climate crisis.

## Confronting the Flames

This isn't the only cinematic exploration of the 2025 L.A. wildfires. The REELZ documentary series **'LA Firestorm'** chronicled the events using firsthand accounts, while PBS's **'Weathered: After the LA Firestorm'** followed survivors as they grappled with recovery and sought answers for the failures that led to such widespread devastation. These projects, alongside Marxt's film, highlight a growing urgency to document and understand these increasingly frequent and intense natural disasters. The shared focus across different platforms underscores the significant impact these fires had and the collective desire to learn from them.

## A Call to Action

For fans of documentary filmmaking and those deeply concerned about climate change, **'>1.5°C: Pyropolitics and the New World'** represents a vital piece of contemporary cinema. It moves beyond abstract data and political debates, presenting the human and environmental cost in stark visual terms. The film's ambition is not merely to document, but to provoke thought and dialogue, encouraging audiences to consider their own role in the face of such crises. It’s a powerful reminder that the "new world" we are rapidly entering is one shaped by our relationship with the environment, and films like Marxt's are essential for navigating it.

## What's Next

Following its premiere at DOK Leipzig and Viennale, **'>1.5°C: Pyropolitics and the New World'** is set to screen at IDFA. Further release details and screening opportunities for audiences worldwide will be announced as they become available.
